processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloyed steels produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots.
Ingots hot-rolled at 1150 °C, obtaining 5 mm flat products.
Hot-rolled flat-products followed by water quenching (part of parent process proc_hot-rolled-1150c).
Samples heat treated (tempered) at 800 °C for 30 min; this is the defining step of process proc_800c-30min-wq.
Heat treatment followed by water quenching ('800 °C heat treatment ... followed by water quenching').

structures.overall_structure: Austenite did not decompose at 800 °C. The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy retained its austenite (FCC_A1) together with δ-ferrite (BCC_A2); no discontinuous precipitation, cellular transformation or spinodal decomposition was triggered, in agreement with the phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)) in which the austenite fraction does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse all alloys at the different processing conditions (hot-rolling and tempering)

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (secondary electron imaging, SEI) with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX/EDS)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM analysis performed only on selected microstructures
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse phase morphologies and chemical compositions; qualitative information on local phase composition

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample

characterization_methods.purpose: Verify consistency of acquired data and highlight chemical composition and process effects

computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic equilibrium calculation (phase volume fraction / amount of all phases vs temperature)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase amounts computed for the 9Al-10Mn-0.4 composition from 0 to 1300 °C; phases BCC_A2, FCC_A1 and KAPPA_E21 tracked (Fig. 9(a)).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated austenite fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C, which explains the observed non-transforming behaviour of austenite at 800 °C; conversely the γ fraction drop from 1150 °C to 600 °C (Fig. 9(a)) corresponds to the discontinuous precipitation observed at 600 °C.

unmapped_findings: The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy underwent austenite decomposition during tempering at 600 °C (Fig. 1(a)) but NOT at 800 °C, even though kinetics should have been faster at 800 °C; the non-transforming behaviour at 800 °C reflects the phase volume fraction diagram (Fig. 9(a)), where the austenite fraction along the red line does not decrease at 800 °C compared to 1150 °C. (b0063, b0064)

No Vickers hardness or any other quantitative property data are reported for the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C composition; all hardness tables (Tables 2, 4, 5, 8, 9) cover other compositions (9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C, 12Al-30Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C), so no measured mechanical property can be attributed to this sample.

Fig. 9 contains an uncaptioned third SEM panel (20 µm scale bar) showing equiaxed grains, dark grain-boundary lines and a horizontal crack/band; its attribution to a specific composition cannot be established from the image alone and is therefore not assigned to this sample.

The general conclusion 'tempering at 800 °C triggered complete and widespread transformations like cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition' (b0117) does NOT apply to the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy, which showed no transformation at 800 °C.
